note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Three VLA limitations motivate MIRTH's three components, each validated by ablations and analyses

nodes.name: Temporal myopia of single-frame VLAs
nodes.description: Most open-source VLAs decode actions from only the current observation and instruction (a Markovian assumption), discarding motion trends and object permanence under occlusion.

nodes.name: Naive history is too costly
nodes.description: Naively extending context windows or using video transformers with dense spatio-temporal attention incurs prohibitive compute, quadratic scaling, large memory and high latency for real-time control.

nodes.name: Dual-scale temporal memory hubs
nodes.description: MIRTH compresses history into fixed-length memory via a workspace hub (K exponential moving averages at different decay rates, mixed with motion-statistics) and a short-horizon hub (attention over the last w frames), fused by a per-patch sigmoid gate; token count stays fixed regardless of history length.

nodes.name: Reasoning gap and many-to-one problem
nodes.description: Prior VLAs map inputs directly to actions (no interpretability or planning) or use hand-crafted discrete action-language supervision, which is costly to annotate and suffers the many-to-one problem where diverse descriptions map to the same motion.

nodes.name: Latent reasoning tokens with MI objective
nodes.description: MIRTH inserts m learnable reasoning tokens between context and action tokens, trained with InfoNCE contrastive losses that pull their representation toward both the action representation and the context representation, without text supervision.

nodes.name: Autoregressive scalar decoding is slow
nodes.description: Scalar-wise quantization of continuous actions needs an autoregressive chain of tokens per action dimension, causing high decoding latency that limits control frequency.

nodes.name: Parallel vector-wise action decoding
nodes.description: MIRTH uses one action token per full action vector (shortening the action sequence by 1/NF) and decodes the whole trajectory in parallel with a two-layer projection head in a single forward pass, trained with an L1 loss.

nodes.name: Strong LIBERO results
nodes.description: MIRTH exceeds 98% on LIBERO spatial, goal and object suites and reaches 95.3% on LIBERO-Long (average 98.1%), versus OpenVLA-OFT's 94.5% on Long and 97.1% average.

nodes.name: Real-world LeRobot gains grow with difficulty
nodes.description: On the LeRobot platform, MIRTH's advantage over baselines widens as task difficulty increases, especially on abstract-instruction reasoning tasks, while maintaining throughput comparable to or above lighter baselines such as OpenVLA.

nodes.name: Memory hub ablation
nodes.description: On LIBERO-Long, removing the workspace hub drops success by 1.3%, removing the short-term hub by 0.9%, and removing both (single-frame) by 2.1%.

nodes.name: Reasoning ablation
nodes.description: On LIBERO-Long, removing the MI loss reduces success by 0.8% and removing the reasoning tokens entirely by 1.4%.

nodes.name: Hubs encode motion dynamics
nodes.description: Linear probes on MIRTH's features give much lower MAE than on OpenVLA for normalized state (0.11 vs 0.32) and velocity (0.04 vs 0.15), showing the hubs encode motion dynamics.

nodes.name: Model uses temporal order
nodes.description: Randomly shuffling the order of history frames in the short-term hub drops LIBERO-Long success from 95.3% to 88.0%, showing the model exploits sequential structure.

nodes.name: Reasoning tokens cluster by task semantics
nodes.description: t-SNE of reasoning embeddings shows clusters by task semantics (e.g., container-opening vs pick-and-place) without task-ID supervision.

nodes.name: Emergent error recovery
nodes.description: On LeRobot failure episodes MIRTH recovers 12.1% of the time versus 8.7% without reasoning tokens and 5.2% for single-frame OpenVLA.

isolated_nodes.name: Prefix and infusion integration
isolated_nodes.description: Memory can be integrated into the current frame by either token prefixing or multiplicative/additive patch infusion, which have complementary advantages.

isolated_nodes.name: Cached inference
isolated_nodes.description: EMA memory updates let the model cache embeddings across timesteps, so each control step only encodes the current frame, updates the hubs and decodes actions in one forward pass.

structural_reasoning: Each of the three identified VLA limitations maps to a design component, evaluated via benchmarks, ablations and targeted probes.
